1929.us: Herbert Hoover took office in March, a month after Chicago's St. Valentine's Day Massacre. In October the stock market crashed, ending the Roaring Twenties boom.
1929.latam: Mexico's Cristero War ended, and Plutarco Elías Calles founded the National Revolutionary Party, forerunner of the PRI. Chile and Peru settled their long Tacna–Arica border dispute.
1929.europe: Mussolini's Italy and the Holy See signed the Lateran Treaty, creating Vatican City. Ramsay MacDonald formed Britain's second Labour government, and experts drew up the Young Plan to ease German reparations.
1929.russia: Stalin expelled his rival Leon Trotsky from the Soviet Union. In December he called for “liquidating the kulaks as a class”, unleashing forced collectivization of the countryside.
1929.mideast: In British-ruled Palestine, riots in August killed about 250 Jews and Arabs, including a massacre of Jews in Hebron. In Arabia, Ibn Saud crushed the Ikhwan revolt at Sabilla.
1929.africa: In southeastern Nigeria, thousands of Igbo women rose against British-appointed chiefs and rumored taxes in the Women's War. Jomo Kenyatta went to London to press Kikuyu land grievances.
1929.india: Bhagat Singh threw low-power bombs into Delhi's Central Legislative Assembly in April. In December, the Congress under Jawaharlal Nehru demanded Purna Swaraj, complete independence from Britain.
1929.china: Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists ruled from Nanjing, where Sun Yat-sen was reburied in a vast mausoleum. A clash over the Chinese Eastern Railway brought Soviet troops into Manchuria.

1930.us: Hoover signed the Smoot–Hawley Tariff in June as unemployment climbed. Clyde Tombaugh discovered Pluto, and in December the Bank of United States collapsed in New York.
1930.latam: Uruguay hosted and won the first football World Cup. Coups ousted Argentina's President Hipólito Yrigoyen and brought Getúlio Vargas to power in Brazil.
1930.europe: In September elections, Hitler's Nazis jumped from 12 to 107 Reichstag seats. Chancellor Heinrich Brüning governed by emergency decree, and the last Allied troops left the Rhineland.
1930.russia: Forced collectivization herded peasants onto collective farms, and families branded kulaks were deported east. Stalin's article “Dizzy with Success” briefly slowed the drive, and the Gulag was founded.
1930.mideast: Britain signed a treaty promising Iraq independence. Turkey made “Istanbul” the city's official name and let women vote in local elections, while Egypt's Ismail Sidqi replaced the constitution.
1930.africa: Ras Tafari was crowned Emperor Haile Selassie of Ethiopia in November. In Liberia, a League of Nations report on forced labor led President Charles King to resign.
1930.india: Gandhi's 24-day Salt March to Dandi defied British law and sparked mass civil disobedience. Tens of thousands were jailed, and London hosted the first Round Table Conference.
1930.china: Chiang Kai-shek defeated rival warlords in the Central Plains War, which left hundreds of thousands of casualties. In Japan, Prime Minister Hamaguchi Osachi was shot after accepting the London Naval Treaty.

1933.us: Franklin D. Roosevelt took office in March, declared a national bank holiday and pushed a burst of New Deal laws through Congress in his first Hundred Days. Prohibition ended in December.
1933.latam: A general strike toppled Cuban dictator Gerardo Machado, and Sergeant Fulgencio Batista rose to power in September's Sergeants' Revolt. Bolivia and Paraguay kept fighting the Chaco War.
1933.europe: Hitler became German chancellor on 30 January. After the Reichstag fire, the Enabling Act let him rule by decree, and Dachau concentration camp opened in March.
1933.russia: Famine killed millions across the Soviet Union, above all in Ukraine and Kazakhstan, as grain was seized from villages. In November the United States formally recognized the Soviet government.
1933.mideast: Saudi Arabia granted an oil concession to Standard Oil of California. In newly independent Iraq, the army massacred Assyrian villagers at Simele, and King Faisal I died in September.
1933.africa: In South Africa, rivals J.B.M. Hertzog and Jan Smuts formed a coalition government. Godfrey Huggins became prime minister of white-ruled Southern Rhodesia, a post he held for two decades.
1933.india: Student Choudhry Rahmat Ali coined the name “Pakistan” in a pamphlet written in Cambridge. Gandhi launched his weekly Harijan and fasted for 21 days in his campaign against untouchability.
1933.china: Japan seized Rehe province and quit the League of Nations over criticism of its Manchurian takeover. Chiang Kai-shek launched his fifth campaign against the Communists' Jiangxi base.

1935.us: Roosevelt signed the Social Security Act and the Wagner Act protecting unions, and the new WPA put millions to work. Senator Huey Long was assassinated in Louisiana in September.
1935.latam: The Chaco War ended in a ceasefire favoring Paraguay. Tango star Carlos Gardel died in a plane crash in Medellín, and Venezuela's longtime dictator Juan Vicente Gómez died in December.
1935.europe: The Saar voted to rejoin Germany, and Hitler restored military conscription in defiance of the Versailles treaty. In September the Nuremberg Laws stripped German Jews of citizenship.
1935.russia: The Moscow Metro opened in May. Miner Alexei Stakhanov's record coal shift launched a campaign to boost output, while arrests spread after the murder of party boss Sergei Kirov.
1935.mideast: Reza Shah asked foreign governments to call Persia “Iran”. In British Palestine, police killed the militant preacher Izz ad-Din al-Qassam, whose death helped spark the 1936 Arab revolt.
1935.africa: Mussolini's Italy invaded Ethiopia in October, and the League of Nations imposed limited sanctions. In Northern Rhodesia, African miners on the Copperbelt struck over a sudden tax increase.
1935.india: An earthquake destroyed Quetta in May, killing tens of thousands. Britain passed the Government of India Act, promising elected provincial governments, and the Reserve Bank of India opened.
1935.china: Mao Zedong gained a leading role at the Zunyi Conference, and the Red Army's Long March ended in Shaanxi in October. In December, students in Peiping (Beijing) protested Japanese encroachment.

1938.us: Superman debuted in Action Comics, and Joe Louis knocked out Max Schmeling in one round. The Fair Labor Standards Act set the first federal minimum wage, 25 cents an hour.
1938.latam: Mexican President Lázaro Cárdenas nationalized foreign oil companies on 18 March, creating the state firm Pemex. In Brazil, Getúlio Vargas's dictatorship crushed an attempted coup by the fascist Integralists.
1938.europe: Germany annexed Austria in March and took the Sudetenland after the Munich Agreement. On Kristallnacht in November, Nazi mobs attacked Jews, synagogues and shops across Germany.
1938.russia: Nikolai Bukharin was convicted in the last Moscow show trial and shot. Soviet troops fought Japan at Lake Khasan, and Lavrentiy Beria took over the NKVD as the purge wound down.
1938.mideast: Drillers struck oil at Dammam in Saudi Arabia and at Burgan in Kuwait. Turkey's founder Mustafa Kemal Atatürk died on 10 November, and the Arab revolt raged on in Palestine.
1938.africa: Afrikaners marked the centenary of the Great Trek with an ox-wagon trek across South Africa, fueling nationalism. Jomo Kenyatta published “Facing Mount Kenya”, a study of Kikuyu life.
1938.india: Subhas Chandra Bose became Congress president at the Haripura session, urging a tougher line against British rule. Congress ministries, elected in 1937, governed most of India's provinces.
1938.china: Nationalist forces won at Taierzhuang, then breached the Yellow River dikes to slow Japan, a flood that killed hundreds of thousands. After Wuhan fell in October, the government retreated to Chongqing.

1939.us: Marian Anderson sang at the Lincoln Memorial after being barred from Constitution Hall, and the New York World's Fair opened. After war began in Europe, Congress allowed cash-and-carry arms sales.
1939.latam: An earthquake destroyed Chillán, Chile, in January, killing about 28,000 people. In December the German warship Admiral Graf Spee was scuttled off Montevideo after the Battle of the River Plate.
1939.europe: Germany seized Prague in March, and Franco won Spain's civil war. Germany invaded Poland on 1 September, and Britain and France declared war two days later.
1939.russia: Stalin signed a pact with Hitler in August and invaded eastern Poland in September. Georgy Zhukov defeated Japan at Khalkhin Gol, and the Winter War with Finland began in November.
1939.mideast: Britain's White Paper capped Jewish immigration to Palestine at 75,000 over five years. France ceded Hatay, part of its Syrian mandate, to Turkey, and Iraq's King Ghazi died in a car crash.
1939.africa: South Africa's parliament voted 80 to 67 to join the war against Germany, and Prime Minister J.B.M. Hertzog, who wanted neutrality, gave way to Jan Smuts. Colonial armies began recruiting across Africa.
1939.india: The viceroy declared India at war without consulting Indian leaders, and Congress provincial governments resigned in protest. Muhammad Ali Jinnah's Muslim League celebrated a “Day of Deliverance” from Congress rule.
1939.china: Japanese bombers pounded the wartime capital Chongqing, killing thousands in May. Chinese forces held Changsha, while former Nationalist leader Wang Jingwei negotiated with Japan to head a collaborationist government.

1947.us: Jackie Robinson broke baseball's color line with the Brooklyn Dodgers. The Truman Doctrine and Marshall Plan launched Cold War containment, and Chuck Yeager flew faster than sound.
1947.latam: Argentina gave women the vote, a cause championed by Eva Perón, who also made a celebrated tour of Europe. Nations of the Americas signed the Rio Treaty, pledging mutual defense.
1947.europe: Britain shivered through a brutal winter of fuel shortages. In June the US offered Marshall Plan aid, and Communists were forced out of the French and Italian governments.
1947.russia: A postwar famine killed a million or more Soviet citizens. Stalin made Eastern Europe reject Marshall Plan aid and founded the Cominform to coordinate Europe's Communist parties.
1947.mideast: The UN voted on 29 November to partition Palestine into Jewish and Arab states, and fighting broke out within days. Bedouin shepherds found the first Dead Sea Scrolls at Qumran.
1947.africa: A revolt against French rule erupted in Madagascar in March; the French crackdown left tens of thousands dead. Kwame Nkrumah returned to the Gold Coast to organize a new nationalist party.
1947.india: On 15 August, British India became independent as India and Pakistan. Partition uprooted about 15 million people and killed hundreds of thousands, and war over Kashmir began in October.
1947.china: Civil war between Nationalists and Communists spread across China. In Taiwan, Nationalist troops crushed the February 28 uprising, and Japan's new pacifist constitution took effect in May.

1950.us: Truman approved work on the hydrogen bomb and sent US troops to Korea in June. Senator Joseph McCarthy's anti-Communist crusade began, and Charles Schulz's Peanuts debuted.
1950.latam: Uruguay stunned Brazil 2–1 at Rio's Maracanã stadium to win the World Cup before nearly 200,000 fans. In Guatemala, Jacobo Árbenz won the presidency promising land reform.
1950.europe: On 9 May, France's Robert Schuman proposed pooling French and West German coal and steel, the seed of today's European Union. The European Convention on Human Rights was signed in November.
1950.russia: Stalin and Mao signed a Sino-Soviet friendship treaty in Moscow. Stalin approved North Korea's invasion of the South, while Soviet diplomats boycotted the UN Security Council.
1950.mideast: Israel passed the Law of Return, giving every Jew the right to immigrate, and Jordan annexed the West Bank. Egypt's Wafd party returned to power after January elections.
1950.africa: South Africa passed the Population Registration and Group Areas acts, classifying people by race and segregating neighborhoods. In the Gold Coast, British authorities jailed Kwame Nkrumah after mass strikes.
1950.india: India became a republic on 26 January as its new constitution took effect, with Rajendra Prasad as president. A magnitude 8.6 earthquake struck Assam and Tibet in August.
1950.china: North Korea invaded the South on 25 June, and Chinese troops entered the war in October. Mao's new government launched land reform and sent the army into Tibet.

1956.us: Eisenhower signed the act creating the Interstate Highway System and won re-election. Elvis Presley became a national sensation, and the Montgomery bus boycott ended after the Supreme Court struck down bus segregation.
1956.latam: Fidel Castro and 81 other rebels landed in Cuba aboard the yacht Granma in December. Brazil's President Juscelino Kubitschek began building Brasília, and Nicaraguan dictator Anastasio Somoza García was assassinated.
1956.europe: Hungarians rose against Soviet-backed rule in October until Soviet tanks crushed the revolution in November. Switzerland hosted the first Eurovision Song Contest in Lugano.
1956.russia: Nikita Khrushchev denounced Stalin's crimes in a secret speech to the 20th Party Congress in February. In November, Soviet forces crushed the Hungarian uprising.
1956.mideast: Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalized the Suez Canal Company, leading to an Israeli, British and French attack. Morocco and Tunisia won independence from France, while Algeria's war of independence intensified.
1956.africa: Sudan became independent on 1 January. In South Africa, 20,000 women marched in Pretoria against pass laws, and in December police arrested 156 activists, including Nelson Mandela, for treason.
1956.india: India redrew its state borders along language lines. B.R. Ambedkar led hundreds of thousands of Dalits in converting to Buddhism, and Pakistan became an Islamic republic under its first constitution.
1956.china: Mao invited open criticism with the Hundred Flowers campaign, launched in May. Japan restored relations with the Soviet Union and joined the United Nations in December.

1957.us: Eisenhower sent troops to protect nine Black students integrating Little Rock's Central High School. Congress passed the first civil rights act since Reconstruction, and Jack Kerouac's On the Road appeared.
1957.latam: François “Papa Doc” Duvalier won Haiti's presidency in September. Colombia's military ruler Gustavo Rojas Pinilla fell in May, and Fidel Castro's rebels fought on in Cuba's Sierra Maestra.
1957.europe: Six nations signed the Treaty of Rome, founding the European Economic Community. Harold Macmillan succeeded Anthony Eden in Britain, telling voters they had “never had it so good”.
1957.russia: Khrushchev beat a Kremlin plot to oust him. The R-7, the first intercontinental missile, launched Sputnik in October, and a nuclear waste tank exploded at the secret Mayak plant.
1957.mideast: The Suez Canal reopened in April after salvage crews cleared it. Tunisia abolished its monarchy and made Habib Bourguiba president, and the Eisenhower Doctrine offered US aid against communism.
1957.africa: On 6 March the Gold Coast became independent Ghana, led by Kwame Nkrumah, inspiring independence movements across the continent. In Kenya, the British hanged Mau Mau leader Dedan Kimathi.
1957.india: Kerala elected a Communist government under E.M.S. Namboodiripad, and Nehru's Congress won India's second general election. Mehboob Khan's Mother India became a landmark of Hindi cinema.
1957.china: When the Hundred Flowers campaign unleashed sharp criticism, Mao launched the Anti-Rightist Campaign, branding over 500,000 people rightists. The first bridge across the Yangtze opened at Wuhan.
